claims.text: Oxidation resistance and material integrity in high-temperature MPEAs are governed by the formation kinetics and quality of the protective oxide layer.
Modest aluminum additions promote formation of a continuous alumina scale.
Modest aluminum additions promote formation of an adherent alumina scale.
An alumina scale acts as a diffusion barrier to oxygen.
The alumina diffusion barrier slows oxidation and preserves the alloy structure.
A continuous and adherent alumina surface scale inhibits transport of oxygen and metal ions.
At high temperature, aluminum diffuses to the alloy surface.
Aluminum preferentially oxidizes because of its high oxygen affinity.
Preferential oxidation of aluminum forms an alumina scale.
The complex chemical environment and sluggish diffusion effects in MPEAs help maintain alumina-scale integrity.
Maintaining alumina-scale integrity reduces further oxidation of the underlying alloy.
Increasing aluminum content will produce a more uniform and adherent alumina scale than in a lower-aluminum baseline.
Increasing aluminum content will lower oxidation rates and oxide-scale thickness relative to the baseline.
Increasing aluminum content will improve retention of mechanical properties relative to the baseline.
The predicted oxidation-resistance improvement will be observable from approximately 700°C to 1000°C.
Oxidation-resistance improvements will show diminishing returns above a critical aluminum concentration.
An MPEA with insufficient aluminum will form a porous, non-protective oxide scale.
The porous, non-protective baseline scale will cause faster oxidation and degradation under otherwise identical conditions.
At temperatures significantly above 1000°C or under non-oxidizing conditions, mechanisms other than protective alumina-scale formation may dominate degradation.
